DEF-WF-IMAGE-TAG.root_cause: Legacy Default.aspx line 53-54 uses the non-standard element followed by a stray with no opening . Browsers parse as and drop the stray , so the migrated renders identically.

FW-ERROR-REDIRECT-BODY.root_cause: CONTRACT.md 3: 3xx bodies (System.Web 'Object moved' HTML vs empty Kestrel redirect) and 4xx/5xx error pages (Mono/System.Web YSOD vs ASP.NET Core error page) are not compared; status and Location are, and match.

FW-HDR-ANTIFORGERY-NOCACHE.root_cause: ASP.NET Core antiforgery marks every response that renders a token no-cache/no-store (+ Pragma: no-cache, Expires: -1) so tokens are never cached; System.Web sends Cache-Control: private. Stricter, no functional effect (every page in the migrated WebForms app carries the layout token).

FW-HDR-BUNDLE-CACHE.root_cause: System.Web.Optimization serves /bundles/* and /Content/css with Cache-Control: public and a one-year Expires; the migrated bundle endpoints return the same content without long-lived caching (performance only).

FW-HDR-CHARSET.root_cause: Mono/System.Web omits the charset parameter, Kestrel adds charset=utf-8; bodies are UTF-8 on both sides (CONTRACT.md: charset ignored).

FW-HDR-COOKIE-NAMES.root_cause: Session and antiforgery cookie names/attributes are framework-specific (ASP.NET_SessionId / __RequestVerificationToken vs .AspNetCore.Session / .AspNetCore.Antiforgery.*, which add httponly/samesite). Values are opaque and never shared between the stacks.

FW-HDR-DEFAULT-PRIVATE.root_cause: System.Web adds Cache-Control: private to every dynamic response by default; Kestrel adds no Cache-Control. Without validators/expiry browsers do not reuse either response.

FW-HDR-REDIRECT-NO-BODY.root_cause: System.Web writes an 'Object moved' HTML body (with content-type) on redirects; ASP.NET Core redirects have no body and therefore no content-type.

FW-HDR-RUNTIME.root_cause: System.Web advertises X-AspNet-Version / X-AspNetMvc-Version (version disclosure, not reproduced); ASP.NET Core static files add Accept-Ranges and ETag. Server header present on both.

FW-HDR-WF-XFRAME-NEW-TOKEN.root_cause: The migrated WebForms layout renders an antiforgery token; ASP.NET Core sends X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN when it issues the first antiforgery cookie of a session. Legacy WebForms (ViewState, no antiforgery) sends none. Hardening only; the storefront is never framed cross-origin.

FW-MARKUP-CANONICAL.root_cause: Only attribute order, class-token order, self-closing slashes, whitespace or HTML character-reference spelling (' vs ', + vs +, & vs &) differ; the parsed DOM is identical (Razor HtmlEncoder vs System.Web encoder).

FW-MVC-BUNDLE-DEBUG.root_cause: Legacy Web.config has <compilation debug="true">, so System.Web.Optimization renders the bundle's individual files; the migrated app references /bundles/jqueryval, which serves the same scripts (static-bundle-jqueryval transcript matches).

FW-MVC-EMPTY-VALIDATION-SUMMARY.root_cause: With only property-level errors, MVC 5 ValidationSummary(true) renders an empty summary container with a hidden <li>; ASP.NET Core renders nothing. Nothing visible in either.

example.migrated: <select class="form-control" data-val-number="The field Brand must be a number." data-val-required="The Brand field is required." data-val="true" id="CatalogBrandId" name="CatalogBrandId">

FW-MVC-SELECT-VALIDATION.root_cause: Legacy uses Html.DropDownList("CatalogBrandId", null) whose metadata resolves to the ViewBag SelectList, so MVC 5 emits no data-val attributes; the migrated DropDownListFor binds the int property and emits required/number rules. Every option is a valid id, so the rules never fire.

FW-WF-LISTVIEW-WRAPPER.root_cause: asp:ListView wraps its output in a <span id=ctl00_MainContent_productList> (control id); the Razor list renders the same table without the wrapper. No CSS/JS targets that id.

FW-WF-POSTBACK-RUNTIME.root_cause: System.Web WebForms postback plumbing (ViewState/EventValidation hidden fields, MS AJAX/WebForms client scripts, form action/ctl00_ ids) has no ASP.NET Core equivalent; the Razor Pages app posts the same form fields with an antiforgery token. Every postback flow (create/edit/delete incl. validation) is covered by the transcripts and matches.

fixed.root_cause: Razor layout/pages rendered fixed 'favicon.ico' / './' links; System.Web ResolveClientUrl renders ~/ relative to the request directory, so on nested routes (/Default/index/0/size/10, /Catalog/Details/1) the favicon, brand and Cancel/Back links pointed under the routed path.
fixed.evidence: favicon.ico vs ../../../../favicon.ico on every nested WebForms route

fixed.root_cause: MVC 5 emitted data-val-number for every numeric property (ClientDataTypeModelValidatorProvider); ASP.NET Core only for float/double/decimal, so Stock/Restock/Max stock/Id lost the client 'must be a number' check.

MVC 5 AntiForgery.GetHtml() sent X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN on every response that rendered a token; ASP.NET Core only when it issues a new antiforgery cookie, so Create/Edit/Delete pages viewed with an existing cookie lost clickjacking protection.
fixed.evidence: x-frame-options missing on 12 MVC token pages (create/edit invalid POSTs, edit GET, delete GET)

fixed.root_cause: Nullable reference types made ASP.NET Core add an implicit [Required] to non-nullable strings (PictureFileName); MVC 5 had no implicit required, so the read-only Picture field gained data-val-required and server-side validation.
Create/Edit/Delete Razor pages rendered a second <form> inside the layout's page-wide Site.Master form; the inner </form> closed the outer form early. Legacy has a single master form.
Validator spans used one class for every field; legacy Name RequiredFieldValidator has CssClass 'field-validation-valid text-danger', the range validators 'text-danger'.
fixed.evidence: span class on WebForms validation messages
